summary: Both transfer-thread suspicions are now refuted with a receipt and a mechanism-level argument, and I have recorded the next lead. The retained interrupted-transfer run did exercise the intended state — target last index 2 against the leader's 202, so the drain loop had real work, and every transfer resolved with 'leadership transfer timeout' rather than completing — yet the in-progress flag was false in all ten interrupted trials, no goroutine was stranded in the transfer path, and in the trials where another node became leader first the interrupted node was re-elected with Apply and GetConfiguration both succeeding; the controls completed cleanly. The decisive reason is source-level: triggerDeferErrorCh is created with capacity 1, and the transfer goroutine only reaches a send after receiving the response to the previous deferError, which means the replicator consumed it, so the buffer is empty at every send and a buffered send never needs a reader — the stranding premise is wrong, not merely unobserved. The parent TimeoutNow suspicion is refuted the same way: the handler validates nothing, but the only internal producer reaches the trans.TimeoutNow call immediately after its drain loop exits, with that loop's exit points all guarded by the transfer stop channel, so no internal path supplies a transfer message that no longer reflects the leader; what remains is a hardening observation (the request carries no term and the receiver checks no sender) rather than a defect. I disclosed the local single-threaded GOMAXPROCS=1 follow-up as native feedback rather than evidence, since the buffer argument does not depend on it. Looking for the next judgment-changing relationship I found a promising one on the same authority axis and recorded it with anchors: verifyLeader seeds votes with the leader's own vote and registers the verify future with every followerReplication — including nonvoters — while quorumSize counts only voters, so a leader partitioned from all other voters but still able to reach a nonvoter can satisfy the voter quorum with an acknowledgement that cannot vote; the discriminator is a three-voter plus one-nonvoter cluster where the leader and the nonvoter are partitioned together, with a control that cuts the nonvoter off as well.
